coverages.description: Live coverage of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest movement — detentions, ultimatums, court cases, INDIA-bloc actions and on-ground developments in Delhi.
coverages.title: CJP Protest 2.0
coverages.current_summary: Das and Ranka's Sunday (Oct 18) SEM hearing ended with no release; on Monday evening a newly-appointed SEM (Ritu Raj) extended their judicial custody two more days till Oct 21 after rejecting their sureties, and Delhi Police transferred both cases (the Oct 13 Jantar Mantar trespass case and the Oct 16 march case) to the Crime Branch's Inter-State Cell. On Wednesday Oct 21 the two withdrew their Delhi High Court plea against the custody extension and were told to await a 2 PM SEM hearing. Dipke's preventive-arrest case ended with his Oct 17 conditional bail (one-year peace bond + Rs 50,000 surety), and on Oct 20 he announced in a video message that CJP will hold no protests at all until Diwali — the day after Diwali (Nov 8) became the resume target. A 30-foot cockroach effigy was burnt alongside Ravana at the Pitampura Dussehra on Oct 20, which Dipke thanked organizers for as 'free publicity.' Rathee's Saturday-noon London rally Oct 17 was ANI-confirmed (polarised turnout), and Saket Court issued a bailable warrant against him in the 2018 defamation case (civil-suit next hearing Nov 5). On Oct 20 former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee called the custody extension 'state-sponsored terrorism' and demanded Das and Ranka's immediate release, echoed by BJD's Naveen Patnaik.

coverages.description: Live coverage of the Houthi-Saudi escalation — missile and drone strikes on Riyadh and oil sites, airport and airspace closures, Saudi/coalition retaliation, US moves and diplomatic developments.
coverages.title: Houthi-Riyadh Escalation
coverages.current_summary: King Khalid International Airport reopened Oct 17 after its week-long closure, but recovery has stalled — GACA NOTAM A3650/26 (no expiry) still requires prior permission for every flight, and most carriers remain grounded. The coalition announced interceptions Oct 17–19 (drones over Riyadh, missiles at Khamis Mushait); Oct 19 brought the Houthis' deadliest strike since July — three ballistic missiles on the Shabwa training camp killing 73 and injuring 200+. On Oct 20-21 the coalition reported intercepting a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh (destroying its launch platform), five drones and a cruise missile over the Medina region; Yemen's armed forces spokesman (government side) claimed 744 strikes in 24 hours under 'Operation Dawn of Yemen', neutralizing ~200 Houthis. Saudi Arabia lost an AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter in Najran on Oct 18 (technical malfunction, 2 crew killed) while a hostile projectile injured six in Najran homes; Egypt's Sisi sought emergency parliament authorization to defend Saudi Arabia (vote postponed to next Monday); the kingdom postponed next week's 'Davos in the Desert' FII; and Saree claimed six Houthi operations in 48 hours against targets including Riyadh airport, Yanbu, Shaybah and Abha. On Oct 20 the UK announced RAF Typhoon defensive missions over Saudi skies, France sent forces to guard the Yanbu oil terminal and 100+ US advisers fell under a new joint command; inside Yemen, a Houthi strike on a Taiz residential area killed two teenage girls (AP), while the Houthis claimed Saudi airstrikes on fishing boats off Taiz killed eight. Brent hit a five-month high ($111.75 intraday Oct 20) on the war risk premium. GCC foreign ministers at the Oct 18 Manama ministerial council condemned the attacks and pushed for a Houthi terrorist designation alongside US-Iran dialogue. On Wednesday morning Oct 21 a Houthi ballistic missile struck near Aden International Airport (explosion heard, smoke rising); Saree meanwhile denied any Wednesday drone launches toward Medina, disputing the coalition's intercept claims.

coverages.description: Live coverage of the Russia-Ukraine war focused on the 'Energy Ceasefire' — strikes on energy infrastructure by either side, ceasefire claims and violations, Kremlin/White House/Kyiv statements, EU sanctions and oil-market fallout.
coverages.title: Russia-Ukraine War & Energy Ceasefire
coverages.current_summary: Trump's 'energy ceasefire' is effectively dead: Ukraine resumed refinery strikes Oct 15 — hours after Zelensky told the FT 'the block is out, we're done' — hitting the Rosneft refinery in Ryazan, and on the night of Oct 17–18 launched its largest drone attack of the war on St. Petersburg (~1,000 drones), setting the Petersburg Oil Terminal ablaze. On Wednesday morning Oct 21 Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin at the Constantine Palace in St. Petersburg (Kushner joined virtually with an updated peace proposal) — an opening goodwill gesture saw Russia release a detained 74-year-old US retiree, and Witkoff cited a 'basis for a ceasefire' aimed at a pathway toward direct trilateral talks. Washington tilted toward Moscow this week: Trump signed an executive order Oct 16 pausing the Graham Act's Russia sanctions (Zelensky called it a 'historic mistake'), and the WSJ reported Putin proposed a Trump–Xi summit on Ukraine — without Kyiv — on the sidelines of the Nov 18–19 APEC summit in Shenzhen (confirmed by the Kremlin Oct 19). On Oct 20, Zelensky met Witkoff in Oslo, saying US intelligence-sharing 'works now'. Overnight Oct 19-20, Ukrainian drones struck Transneft's Nikolskoye-1 pumping station in Tambov — a Druzhba-network hub — sparking a fuel-tank fire (Governor Pervyshov confirmed). On Oct 19 a Russian drone struck a park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv region, killing six including three children, while 22 bipartisan House lawmakers urged Trump (Oct 15 letter) to revoke the Russian diesel import licence. Overnight Oct 20–21, Russian strikes hit energy facilities in Kyiv, Volyn, Odesa and Mykolaiv regions, killing four — hours ahead of the Witkoff-Putin meeting. On Oct 20 Zelensky told Corriere della Sera Ukraine backs a mutual energy ceasefire if the US supplies interceptor missiles to defend its grid — and told US senators the Pentagon is holding up European-paid air-defense missiles pending Hegseth's signature, with Kyiv down to 'only a couple' of Patriot interceptors (WaPo).

coverages.description: Live coverage of hurricane and tropical-storm activity impacting North America — NHC advisories, storm formation and intensity changes, watches and warnings, landfalls, casualties, damage and outage numbers, evacuations, closures and recovery.
coverages.location: North America (Atlantic basin, Gulf of Mexico, US Gulf/East coasts, Mexico's Pacific coast)
coverages.title: Hurricane Activity Impacting North America
coverages.current_summary: Tropical Storm Trudy formed off southern Mexico on Oct 13 (40 mph in NHC Advisory 2, ~490 mi SSE of Acapulco) with rapid intensification to a major hurricane forecast by Friday; Hurricane Simon re-strengthened to 110 mph, nearly a major hurricane again, after mainland Mexico watches were lifted (Advisory 26) and Puerto Vallarta airport reopened — NHC's discussion shifted Simon's track to a weekend coast approach with a possible Sunday inland crossing over Sonora; Tropical Storm Trudy (45 mph) had its track nudged east, putting a major-hurricane landfall threat on western Mexico this weekend — while damage tallies keep rising across Guerrero, Colima and Baja California Sur, with Ensenada's death toll from Tropical Cyclone Rachel's remnant flooding reaching 7 on Tuesday Oct 13. The White House approved federal emergency declarations for Florida and Alabama ahead of Isaias's landfall; no active Atlantic cyclones after the Cabo Verde disturbance fizzled. Isaias recovery reached ~95% of impacted-area customers restored as of Tuesday evening (~57,000 still out), Florida rolled out $10M in zero-interest business loans plus farm loans and SNAP aid for the Panhandle, and catastrophe modeler Verisk issued the first industry insured-loss estimate: $1B–$2B for onshore property. DeSantis also raised Florida's storm-related death toll to six; by Wednesday Oct 14 the storm-wide toll reached nine, after the Greenwood County coroner reported 67-year-old Christopher John Miller died Oct 11 when a tree fell on his home in Ninety Six, South Carolina, during Isaias's remnants; by Wednesday morning Oct 14, just over 20,000 customers remained without power — mainly Escambia and Santa Rosa counties — down from 45,000+ Tuesday. Wednesday's NHC updates (Oct 14): Hurricane Simon dipped to 105 mph and drifted southwestward — NHC calls it 'compact' — keeping the weekend coast-approach threat for Sonora; Tropical Storm Trudy strengthened to 50 mph with the track shifted west, and is now expected to reach hurricane strength within 24 hours. Latest NHC advisories (Wed Oct 14, 8-9 AM MST/CST): Hurricane Simon weakened to 90 mph (Category 1), drifting southwestward; Mexico dropped its last coastal watch, leaving no coastal watches or warnings in effect for now, though Baja California Sur watches may be required in the next day or two; Tropical Storm Trudy strengthened to 60 mph and is now expected to become a hurricane tonight and a major hurricane by Friday.

coverages.title: U.S.–Iran Conflict & Strait of Hormuz
coverages.description: Live coverage of the U.S.–Iran confrontation — military posturing, strikes or threats, Strait of Hormuz shipping incidents and closure threats, Iranian statements, US administration moves, oil-market and diplomatic fallout.
coverages.current_summary: Mine warfare in the Strait of Hormuz escalated sharply: the IRGC Navy said two oil tankers (~2M barrels each) were set ablaze by mines on Oct 17 and two more 'non-compliant' tankers on Oct 20, warning oil companies of a 'heavier price'; Kpler counted at least 18 vessel attacks in the fortnight to Oct 20, and Brent touched a five-month high (~$112, settling ~$109) on Oct 20–21. On Oct 21 morning a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile 11 nm west of Oman's Bukha — the fire was extinguished and the crew is safe — while WSJ/Kpler data for the week ending Oct 18 showed Gulf oil exports actually topped prewar levels despite the attacks. On Oct 19 Iran claimed US forces struck the Konarak naval base wounding two — the first alleged US strike on Iranian soil since Sept 1 — which Washington disputes. CNN reported Oct 19 (multiple US officials) that the US military has drawn up new Iran strike plans including possible use of the GBU-43/B 'MOAB' on energy and nuclear targets if Trump resumes combat before or after Nov 3; advisers are privately unsure his no-strike pledge is definitive. Diplomacy crept back on Oct 18: FM Abbas Araqchi said Tehran's offer to reopen the strait within six days remains on the table if Washington lifts the port blockade, ends oil-export sanctions and hostilities; on Oct 19 Araqchi mocked Trump's 'soon finish the job' warning on X and accused Netanyahu of pushing the US into war; on Oct 21, IMO chief Arsenio Dominguez said mines remain on the approved traffic-separation route and the agency cannot declare it safe. On Oct 20, Iranian armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi warned any renewed attack would draw a 'much stronger and more forceful response', while Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused Iran of 'Nazi U-boat tactics' against commercial shipping and called a deal 'tough'. On Oct 20 Qatar and Pakistan proposed Iran receive the interest earned on ~$6B of frozen funds in Qatari banks in exchange for confidential IAEA inspections; Araghchi said the strait stays closed until Washington accepts Tehran's conditions. On Oct 19 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Israel, discussing Iran with Netanyahu.

coverages.title: 2026 US Midterm Elections
coverages.description: Polls, early voting, key House/Senate/gubernatorial races, and campaign moves ahead of the Nov 3, 2026 US midterm elections.
coverages.current_summary: Two weeks out, Sabato's Crystal Ball moved 28 House races toward Democrats on Oct 20 — first post-218 projection: Democrats favoured in 223 races, Republicans 200, 12 toss-ups — while the Senate tightens: a CBS News/YouGov poll (Oct 18) has Talarico 51, Paxton 49 in Texas, and Georgia's governor race is effectively tied (AJC/UGA: Jackson 46, Bottoms 45). On Oct 19 the DOJ filed an emergency motion in Central District of California court (United States v. California, No. 2:26-cv-12025) seeking to freeze ~20,000 mail ballots, and charged 28 people in 'Operation Protect the Vote' the same day; the RNC countered by expanding its vote-protection operation (directors in 22 states, 21,500 poll workers, 179 active cases). Trump held his Wichita, KS rally Oct 19 (announcing $8B in one-time farmer payments to offset Iran-war diesel prices) and Greenville, NC Oct 20 (nearly 2-hour speech), part of a cash-pitch closing strategy — $30K government-fraud tips, $5,000 checks if the GOP wins — with Fort Myers, FL (confirmed for Fri Oct 23 at FGCU's Alico Arena, plus a second planned Florida rally), Clemson, Iowa, Macon and Lubbock ahead. Early voting is surging: Texas shattered first-day records Oct 19 (Harris County 104,600+ in-person), Georgia passed 1M ballots (+12% vs 2022), Michigan hit 789,572 ballots (mail requests +17% vs 2022), and Florida's first-day early vote nearly doubled in Orange County with 2.6M ballots already returned across four states plus Pima County; Sanders and O'Rourke kicked off a Texas early-voting tour Oct 19–20 while Talarico held his own events. Georgia GOP governor nominee Rick Jackson will skip Trump's Macon rally on Sat Oct 24, and Barack Obama will headline a 'United for Georgia' rally in Atlanta on Oct 28 for Ossoff and Bottoms. An Oct 18 Post-ABC News/Ipsos poll put Trump's approval at 33%, a record low, with Democrats +8 on the House ballot (52-44); NBC's Decision Desk poll the same day found 34% approval and 55-45 preferring Democratic congressional control. Prediction markets (DeFi Rate, Oct 21): Democrats 65% for the Senate (+2 pts on the week), 91% for the House (+1). New polls Oct 21: CNN/SSRS has Democrats +10 on the congressional-district vote (Trump's CNN approval at a record-low 32%); Reuters/Ipsos has Trump at a record-low 31% with Democrats +12 on the generic ballot. Trump said Oct 20 he has spent or will spend 'over $400M' on the GOP midterms while the NYT reports Bloomberg is putting $80M behind Democrats; and a WaPo investigation found ~10 current/former national-security officials quietly advising ~10 states on possible Trump election interference.

coverages.description: Live coverage of the French protest movement that began with Paris lycée student blockades in September 2026 and escalated into nationwide cost-of-living demonstrations — marches, clashes, arrests and injuries, union and student actions, government response, and the parliamentary budget fight.
coverages.title: Paris Protests — France Cost-of-Living Unrest
coverages.current_summary: The Oct 17 national day of action (550k–800k nationwide, 110k in Paris) gave way to a post-crisis standoff: Lecornu imposed partial/localized curfews on Oct 19 (Paris protest bans, République 11pm–6am curfew, minors' curfews in several cities) and met union leaders at Matignon on Wednesday Oct 21 at 10:30 AM, with party leaders due Thursday Oct 22 at 2:30 PM, while the budget revenue-side vote was postponed to Oct 27. France Info confirmed Oct 21 that two people died in Paris during the Oct 17–18 unrest, alongside the Interior Ministry's consolidated toll: 2,397 arrests, 997 security-forces injured (seven seriously). Accountability moves landed Oct 20: Interior Minister Nuñez apologized in the Assembly ('I accept my share of responsibility') as parliament launched an inquiry commission (200 investigators), and the suspected principal arsonist of the Limoges town-hall fire was arrested at dawn by the RAID (SDAT anti-terror co-seized). The Matignon talks opened Oct 21 with CGT chief Sophie Binet demanding 'political answers' and the CGT set to decide Wednesday on joining the Oct 24 demos; the student coordination (CNL, 27 cities) issued a communique Oct 21 calling for a Paris march on Thursday Oct 22 (2 PM, Salpêtrière to Bastille) and announcing a new national coordination. Ahead of Saturday Oct 24's 'Act II' demos — called by yellow-vest groups (Oct 24 + Oct 31) and backed by five unions striking Nov 5 — Nuñez announced Sentinelle troops, BRI/GIGN/RAID, helicopters and possible bans on non-notified demonstrations. On Oct 20 Toulouse became the first city to impose an all-ages nighttime curfew (hypercentre 11:59 PM-5 AM, Oct 22-25), while Marseille extended its hypercentre/shopping-district curfew (minors 10 PM-5 AM) through Oct 23. Unrest spread overseas: two gendarmerie mobile squadrons deployed in La Réunion (Centaure armor, helicopter) with urban violence also reported in Martinique and Guadeloupe. Correction: the OTRE/FAI trucker mobilization planned for Oct 21-22 was suspended Oct 16 after government concessions and is NOT happening. On Wednesday morning Oct 21 the Oct 17 movement's coordination declared the Oct 24 Paris 'Act II' route: Bastille to Opera.
